sanskrit: jānāti hi sadā bhīṣmaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ yaśasvinām balavattāṃ saputrāṇāṃ dharmajñānāṃ mahātmanām
english: For Bhīṣma always knows the might of those illustrious Pāṇḍavas together with their sons — great-souled ones who are versed in righteousness.

sanskrit: yato nārocayam ahaṃ vigrahaṃ tair mahātmabhiḥ kiṃ tu saṃjaya me brūhi punas teṣāṃ viceṣṭitam
english: It is for this reason that I have never approved of war with those great-souled ones. But, Sañjaya, tell me again of their doings.

sanskrit: kas tāṃs tarasvino bhūyaḥ saṃdīpayati pāṇḍavān arciṣmato maheṣvāsān haviṣā pāvakān iva
english: Who is it that keeps inflaming those vigorous Pāṇḍavas — those blazing great bowmen — as one feeds fire with oblations?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ sadaivaitān saṃdīpayati bhārata yudhyadhvam iti mā bhaiṣṭa yuddhād bharatasattamāḥ
english: Sañjaya said: It is Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O Bhārata, who constantly inflames them, saying, "Fight! Do not fear battle, O best of Bhāratas!"

sanskrit: ye ke cit pārthivās tatra dhārtarāṣṭreṇa saṃvṛtāḥ yuddhe samāgamiṣyanti tumule kavacahrade
english: Whatever kings are there, assembled under the banner of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, will come together in battle — in the tumultuous sea of armour.

sanskrit: tān sarvān āhave kruddhān sānubandhān samāgatān aham ekaḥ samādāsye timir matsyān ivaudakān
english: All of them gathered there in battle — enraged, along with their allies — I alone shall swallow, as a fish-eating reptile swallows fish in the water.

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ droṇaṃ kṛpaṃ karṇaṃ drauṇiṃ śalyaṃ suyodhanam etāṃś cāpi nirotsyāmi veleva makarālayam
english: Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Karṇa, Droṇa's son, Śalya, and Suyodhana — all of these I shall check, as the shore restrains the ocean that is home to sea-monsters.

sanskrit: tathā bruvāṇaṃ dharmātmā prāha rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ tava dhairyaṃ ca vīryaṃ ca pāñcālāḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ saha sarve samadhirūḍhāḥ sma saṃgrāmān naḥ samuddhara
english: As he spoke thus, the righteous king Yudhiṣṭhira addressed him: "Upon your courage and valour, all the Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas are fully resting — rescue us in battle."

sanskrit: jānāmi tvāṃ mahābāho kṣatradharme vyavasthitam samartham ekaṃ paryāptaṃ kauravāṇāṃ yuyutsatām bhavatā yad vidhātavyaṃ tan naḥ śreyaḥ paraṃtapa
english: "I know you, O mighty-armed one, as one firmly established in the warrior's duty, capable alone and sufficient against the Kauravas who desire battle. Whatever you shall ordain will be our good, O scorcher of foes."

sanskrit: saṃgrāmād apayātānāṃ bhagnānāṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇām pauruṣaṃ darśayañ śūro yas tiṣṭhed agrataḥ pumān krīṇīyāt taṃ sahasreṇa nītiman nāma tat padam
english: "The hero who stands in the forefront, showing his manliness when the routed are fleeing from battle and the broken are seeking refuge — a wise man would purchase such a man with a thousand. That indeed is the mark of nobility."

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ śūraś ca vīraś ca vikrāntaś ca nararṣabha bhayārtānāṃ paritrātā saṃyugeṣu na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Such are you — a hero, a warrior, and one of conquering valour, O bull among men. You are undoubtedly the protector of those afflicted by fear in battles."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kaunteye dharmātmani yudhiṣṭhire dhṛṣṭadyumna uvācedaṃ māṃ vaco gatasādhvasaḥ
english: While the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira, son of Kuntī, was speaking thus, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, freed from all fear, spoke these words to me.

sanskrit: sarvāñ janapadān sūta yodhā duryodhanasya ye sabāhlīkān kurūn brūyāḥ prātipeyāñ śaradvataḥ
english: "O charioteer, go and tell all those warriors of Duryodhana in every province — the Kurus together with the Bāhlīkas, and the descendants of Pratīpa, and the son of Sharadvan."

sanskrit: sūtaputraṃ tathā droṇaṃ sahaputraṃ jayadratham duḥśāsanaṃ vikarṇaṃ ca tathā duryodhanaṃ nṛpam
english: "And likewise the son of a charioteer (Karṇa), and Droṇa together with his son, and Jayadratha, and Duḥśāsana, and Vikarṇa, and the king Duryodhana."

sanskrit: bhīṣmaṃ caiva brūhi gatvā tvam āśu; yudhiṣṭhiraṃ sādhunaivābhyupeta mā vo vadhīd arjuno devaguptaḥ; kṣipraṃ yācadhvaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ lokavīram
english: "Go quickly and tell Bhīṣma too: approach Yudhiṣṭhira with good faith only. Let not Arjuna, guarded by the gods, slay you. Quickly supplicate that Pāṇḍava, the hero of the world."

sanskrit: naitādṛśo hi yodho 'sti pṛthivyām iha kaś cana yathāvidhaḥ savyasācī pāṇḍavaḥ śastravittamaḥ
english: "For there is no warrior on this earth such as the ambidextrous Pāṇḍava (Arjuna) — the most knowledgeable of weapons."

sanskrit: devair hi saṃbhṛto divyo ratho gāṇḍīvadhanvanaḥ na sa jeyo manuṣyeṇa mā sma kṛdhvaṃ mano yudhi
english: "For the divine chariot of the Gāṇḍīva-wielder was furnished by the gods — he cannot be conquered by any mortal. Do not set your heart on battle."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca kṣatratejā brahmacārī kaumārād api pāṇḍavaḥ tena saṃyugam eṣyanti mandā vilapato mama
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: That Pāṇḍava (Arjuna) has the martial fire of a warrior and has been a celibate student from his very boyhood. Only the foolish — who lament like me — would go to battle against him.

sanskrit: duryodhana nivartasva yuddhād bharatasattama na hi yuddhaṃ praśaṃsanti sarvāvastham ariṃdama
english: "Turn back from war, O Duryodhana, O best of the Bhāratas. War is not to be praised in any and every circumstance, O subduer of foes."

sanskrit: alam ardhaṃ pṛthivyās te sahāmātyasya jīvitum prayaccha pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ yathocitam ariṃdama
english: "Half of the earth is enough for you and your ministers to live upon. Give to the sons of Pāṇḍu what is rightfully theirs, O subduer of foes."

sanskrit: etad dhi kuravaḥ sarve manyante dharmasaṃhitam yat tvaṃ praśāntim icchethāḥ pāṇḍuputrair mahātmabhiḥ
english: "All the Kurus consider it to be in accord with righteousness that you should seek peace with the great-souled sons of Pāṇḍu."

sanskrit: aṅgemāṃ samavekṣasva putra svām eva vāhinīm jāta eva tava srāvas tvaṃ tu mohān na budhyase
english: "Come, my son, and look at your own army. Your forces have been wasting away from the very moment of your birth, but you do not perceive it out of delusion."

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ yuddham icchāmi naitad icchati bāhlikaḥ na ca bhīṣmo na ca droṇo nāśvatthāmā na saṃjayaḥ
english: "For I do not desire war, nor does Bāhlika desire it, nor Bhīṣma, nor Droṇa, nor Aśvatthāman, nor Sañjaya."

sanskrit: na somadatto na śalyo na kṛpo yuddham icchati satyavrataḥ purumitro jayo bhūriśravās tathā
english: "Neither Somadatta, nor Śalya, nor Kṛpa desires war, nor do Satyavrata, Purumitra, Jaya, and Bhūriśravas."

sanskrit: yeṣu saṃpratitiṣṭheyuḥ kuravaḥ pīḍitāḥ paraiḥ te yuddhaṃ nābhinandanti tat tubhyaṃ tāta rocatām
english: "Those very men upon whom the Kurus would rely when pressed hard by their enemies — those men do not welcome war. Let that, my son, please you as well."

sanskrit: na tvaṃ karoṣi kāmena karṇaḥ kārayitā tava duḥśāsanaś ca pāpātmā śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ
english: "You do not act of your own will — it is Karṇa who makes you act, and the wicked-souled Duḥśāsana, and Śakuni the son of Subala."

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca nāhaṃ bhavati na droṇe nāśvatthāmni na saṃjaye na vikarṇe na kāmboje na kṛpe na ca bāhlike
english: Duryodhana said: I place no burden — neither on you, nor on Droṇa, nor on Aśvatthāman, nor on Sañjaya, nor on Vikarṇa, nor on the Kāmboja king, nor on Kṛpa, nor on Bāhlika.

sanskrit: satyavrate purumitre bhūriśravasi vā punaḥ anyeṣu vā tāvakeṣu bhāraṃ kṛtvā samāhvaye
english: "Nor on Satyavrata, nor on Purumitra, nor again on Bhūriśravas, nor on any others of your party do I lay a burden — and yet I give challenge."

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca tāta karṇaś ca raṇayajñaṃ vitatya vai yudhiṣṭhiraṃ paśuṃ kṛtvā dīkṣitau bharatarṣabha
english: "I and Karṇa, O father, having spread the sacrificial battle and made Yudhiṣṭhira the sacrificial victim, are consecrated for it, O bull of the Bhāratas."

sanskrit: ratho vedī sruvaḥ khaḍgo gadā sruk kavacaṃ sadaḥ cāturhotraṃ ca dhuryā me śarā darbhā havir yaśaḥ
english: "The chariot is the sacrificial altar; the sword is the ladle; the mace is the large spoon; the armour is the assembly hall; the four-priest rite is my chariot-team; my arrows are the sacrificial grass; glory is the oblation."

sanskrit: ātmayajñena nṛpate iṣṭvā vaivasvataṃ raṇe vijitya svayam eṣyāvo hatāmitrau śriyā vṛtau
english: "By this self-sacrifice, O king, having worshipped Yama (son of Vivasvat) in battle, the two of us shall return in victory, having slain our enemies, clothed in glory."

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca tāta karṇaś ca bhrātā duḥśāsanaś ca me ete vayaṃ haniṣyāmaḥ pāṇḍavān samare trayaḥ
english: "I, Karṇa, and my brother Duḥśāsana — the three of us will slay the Pāṇḍavas in battle, O father."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi pāṇḍavān hatvā praśāstā pṛthivīm imām māṃ vā hatvā pāṇḍuputrā bhoktāraḥ pṛthivīm imām
english: "For either I, having slain the Pāṇḍavas, will rule this earth, or the sons of Pāṇḍu, having slain me, will enjoy this earth."

sanskrit: tyaktaṃ me jīvitaṃ rājan dhanaṃ rājyaṃ ca pārthiva na jātu pāṇḍavaiḥ sārdhaṃ vaseyam aham acyuta
english: "I have renounced life, O king, and wealth and kingdom, O lord of the earth. I shall never, ever dwell together with the Pāṇḍavas, O Acyuta."

sanskrit: yāvad dhi sūcyās tīkṣṇāyā vidhyed agreṇa māriṣa tāvad apy aparityājyaṃ bhūmer naḥ pāṇḍavān prati
english: "Even as much land as a sharp needle's tip could pierce — that much, O venerable one, is not to be relinquished by us to the Pāṇḍavas."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sarvān vas tāta śocāmi tyakto duryodhano mayā ye mandam anuyāsyadhvaṃ yāntaṃ vaivasvatakṣayam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: I grieve for all of you, my son — Duryodhana has been abandoned by me, and those who will slowly follow him as he walks to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: rurūṇām iva yūtheṣu vyāghrāḥ praharatāṃ varāḥ varān varān haniṣyanti sametā yudhi pāṇḍavāḥ
english: "As tigers — the foremost of those who strike — slay the finest among herds of deer, so the Pāṇḍavas, assembled together in battle, will slay the best of your men one by one."

sanskrit: pratīpam iva me bhāti yuyudhānena bhāratī vyastā sīmantinī trastā pramṛṣṭā dīrghabāhunā
english: "It seems to me as something running against the current — that the wife of Bhārata (Draupadī), her hair parted, was flung down, terrified, and dishonoured by the long-armed one (Duḥśāsana)."

sanskrit: saṃpūrṇaṃ pūrayan bhūyo balaṃ pārthasya mādhavaḥ śaineyaḥ samare sthātā bījavat pravapañ śarān
english: "Mādhava (Kṛṣṇa) will go on replenishing the already full strength of Pārtha's forces, and Sātyaki, the descendant of Śini, will stand in battle, scattering arrows like seeds."

sanskrit: senāmukhe prayuddhānāṃ bhīmaseno bhaviṣyati taṃ sarve saṃśrayiṣyanti prākāram akutobhayam
english: "Bhīmasena will be at the front of those fighting at the van of the army — all will take shelter in him as a rampart that fears nothing."

sanskrit: yadā drakṣyasi bhīmena kuñjarān vinipātitān viśīrṇadantān giryābhān bhinnakumbhān saśoṇitān
english: "When you shall see elephants felled by Bhīma — their tusks shattered, like mountains in collapse, their foreheads split and streaming with blood —"

sanskrit: tān abhiprekṣya saṃgrāme viśīrṇān iva parvatān bhīto bhīmasya saṃsparśāt smartāsi vacanasya me
english: "— beholding them in battle, fallen like mountains, and in dread of the onslaught of Bhīma, you will remember my words."

sanskrit: nirdagdhaṃ bhīmasenena sainyaṃ hatarathadvipam gatim agner iva prekṣya smartāsi vacanasya me
english: "When you behold your army burnt down by Bhīmasena — its chariots and elephants destroyed, looking like a fire's path — you will remember my words."

sanskrit: mahad vo bhayam āgāmi na cec chāmyatha pāṇḍavaiḥ gadayā bhīmasenena hatāḥ śamam upaiṣyatha
english: "Great danger is coming upon you. If you do not make peace with the Pāṇḍavas, then slain by Bhīmasena's mace, you will attain peace (only in death)."

sanskrit: mahāvanam iva chinnaṃ yadā drakṣyasi pātitam balaṃ kurūṇāṃ saṃgrāme tadā smartāsi me vacaḥ
english: "When you see the Kuru forces cut down and fallen in battle like a great forest felled, then you will remember my words."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etāvad uktvā rājā tu sa sarvān pṛthivīpatīn anubhāṣya mahārāja punaḥ papraccha saṃjayam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus much and addressed all those kings, the king again questioned Sañjaya, O great king.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yad abrūtāṃ mahātmānau vāsudevadhanaṃjayau tan me brūhi mahāprājña śuśrūṣe vacanaṃ tava
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Tell me what those two great-souled ones, Vāsudeva and Dhanañjaya, said to each other — O greatly wise one, I am eager to hear your words.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājan yathā dṛṣṭau mayā kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau ūcatuś cāpi yad vīrau tat te vakṣyāmi bhārata
english: Sañjaya said: Listen, O king, to how I saw Kṛṣṇa and Dhanañjaya, and what those two heroes said to each other — that I shall tell you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pādāṅgulīr abhiprekṣan prayato 'haṃ kṛtāñjaliḥ śuddhāntaṃ prāviśaṃ rājann ākhyātuṃ naradevayoḥ
english: "Keeping my eyes fixed on the tips of my toes, with reverence and hands joined in salutation, I entered the inner chamber, O king, to deliver the message to those two lords of men."

sanskrit: naivābhimanyur na yamau taṃ deśam abhiyānti vai yatra kṛṣṇau ca kṛṣṇā ca satyabhāmā ca bhāminī
english: "Neither Abhimanyu nor the twins (Nakula and Sahadeva) approach that place where the two Kṛṣṇas (Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna) were, and where the beautiful Draupadī and Satyabhāmā were."

sanskrit: ubhau madhvāsavakṣībāv ubhau candanarūṣitau sragviṇau varavastrau tau divyābharaṇabhūṣitau
english: "Both had drunk madhu and asava liquors; both were smeared with sandalwood paste; both wore garlands, excellent garments, and were adorned with divine ornaments."

sanskrit: naikaratnavicitraṃ tu kāñcanaṃ mahad āsanam vividhāstaraṇāstīrṇaṃ yatrāsātām ariṃdamau
english: "There was a great golden seat, variegated with many kinds of gems and spread with diverse coverings, where those two subdurers of foes were seated."

sanskrit: arjunotsaṅgagau pādau keśavasyopalakṣaye arjunasya ca kṛṣṇāyāṃ satyāyāṃ ca mahātmanaḥ
english: "I noticed that Keśava's feet rested in Arjuna's lap, and those of the great-souled Arjuna were in (the laps of) Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) and Satyā (Satyabhāmā)."

sanskrit: kāñcanaṃ pādapīṭhaṃ tu pārtho me prādiśat tadā tad ahaṃ pāṇinā spṛṣṭvā tato bhūmāv upāviśam
english: "Pārtha then pointed me to a golden footstool; I touched it with my hand and sat down on the ground."

sanskrit: ūrdhvarekhatalau pādau pārthasya śubhalakṣaṇau pādapīṭhād apahṛtau tatrāpaśyam ahaṃ śubhau
english: "I then saw, drawn away from the footstool, the two auspicious feet of Pārtha, with upward-rising lines on their soles — bearing auspicious marks."

sanskrit: śyāmau bṛhantau taruṇau śālaskandhāv ivodgatau ekāsanagatau dṛṣṭvā bhayaṃ māṃ mahad āviśat
english: "Upon seeing those two dark, large, youthful (feet) — rising like the trunks of sala trees, placed together on one seat — great fear came over me."

sanskrit: indraviṣṇusamāv etau mandātmā nāvabudhyate saṃśrayād droṇabhīṣmābhyāṃ karṇasya ca vikatthanāt
english: "These two are equal to Indra and Viṣṇu — the dull-minded do not perceive this, owing to their dependence on Droṇa and Bhīṣma and the boastfulness of Karṇa."

sanskrit: nideśasthāv imau yasya mānasas tasya setsyate saṃkalpo dharmarājasya niścayo me tadābhavat
english: "These two are under whose command — in the mind of that man (Yudhiṣṭhira), the resolve of the righteous king will succeed. This conviction came to me then."

sanskrit: satkṛtaś cānnapānābhyām ācchanno labdhasatkriyaḥ añjaliṃ mūrdhni saṃdhāya tau saṃdeśam acodayam
english: "Honoured with food and drink, covered (with hospitality), having received proper courtesies, I joined my palms above my head and prompted those two with (my) message."

sanskrit: dhanurbāṇocitenaikapāṇinā śubhalakṣaṇam pādam ānamayan pārthaḥ keśavaṃ samacodayat
english: "With one hand, accustomed to bow and arrows, bowing to the auspicious foot (of Kṛṣṇa), Pārtha prompted Keśava (to speak)."

sanskrit: indraketur ivotthāya sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ indravīryopamaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ saṃviṣṭo mābhyabhāṣata
english: "Rising like Indra's banner, adorned with all ornaments, Kṛṣṇa — whose valour is comparable to Indra's — being seated (again), addressed me."

sanskrit: vācaṃ sa vadatāṃ śreṣṭho hlādinīṃ vacanakṣamām trāsanīṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ mṛdupūrvāṃ sudāruṇām
english: "He, the foremost of speakers, (spoke) a speech that was pleasing, capable of expression, terrifying to the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, gentle at first, and utterly formidable."

sanskrit: vācaṃ tāṃ vacanārhasya śikṣākṣarasamanvitām aśrauṣam aham iṣṭārthāṃ paścād dhṛdayaśoṣiṇīm
english: "That speech of one worthy to speak — properly syllabled and enunciated, pleasing in purport at first, but in the end withering to the heart — I heard."

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca saṃjayedaṃ vaco brūyā dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ manīṣiṇam śṛṇvataḥ kurumukhyasya droṇasyāpi ca śṛṇvataḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: Sañjaya, speak these words to the wise Dhṛtarāṣṭra — in the presence of the chief of the Kurus, and also in the presence of Droṇa who is listening.

sanskrit: yajadhvaṃ vipulair yajñair viprebhyo datta dakṣiṇāḥ putrair dāraiś ca modadhvaṃ mahad vo bhayam āgatam
english: "Worship with great sacrifices; give fees to the Brāhmaṇas; take joy in your sons and wives — great danger has come upon you."

sanskrit: arthāṃs tyajata pātrebhyaḥ sutān prāpnuta kāmajān priyaṃ priyebhyaś carata rājā hi tvarate jaye
english: "Bestow wealth upon deserving recipients; beget sons born of desire; show affection to those who are dear to you — for the king hastens toward victory."

sanskrit: ṛṇam etat pravṛddhaṃ me hṛdayān nāpasarpati yad govindeti cukrośa kṛṣṇā māṃ dūravāsinam
english: "This debt has grown large and does not depart from my heart — that Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) cried out to me, 'O Govinda!' while I dwelt far away."

sanskrit: tejomayaṃ durādharṣaṃ gāṇḍīvaṃ yasya kārmukam maddvitīyena teneha vairaṃ vaḥ savyasācinā
english: "The enmity you have is with the ambidextrous Arjuna, whose bow is the Gāṇḍīva — blazing with energy and invincible — and who has me as his second."

sanskrit: maddvitīyaṃ punaḥ pārthaṃ kaḥ prārthayitum icchati yo na kālaparīto vāpy api sākṣāt puraṃdaraḥ
english: "Who, unless he is already claimed by Death — or even Indra himself in person — wishes to challenge Pārtha who has me as his second?"

sanskrit: bāhubhyām udvahed bhūmiṃ dahet kruddha imāḥ prajāḥ pātayet tridivād devān yo 'rjunaṃ samare jayet
english: "Whoever would conquer Arjuna in battle could lift the earth with his arms, could burn these creatures in his wrath, could hurl the gods down from the three heavens."

sanskrit: devāsuramanuṣyeṣu yakṣagandharvabhogiṣu na taṃ paśyāmy ahaṃ yuddhe pāṇḍavaṃ yo 'bhyayād raṇe
english: "Among gods, demons, men, Yakṣas, Gandharvas, and serpents — I do not see one who could approach the Pāṇḍava in battle, who could oppose him in combat."

sanskrit: yat tad virāṭanagare śrūyate mahad adbhutam ekasya ca bahūnāṃ ca paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: "What was heard of at the city of Virāṭa — that great and wonderful feat of one against many — that is sufficient proof."

sanskrit: ekena pāṇḍuputreṇa virāṭanagare yadā bhagnāḥ palāyanta diśaḥ paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: "When by a single son of Pāṇḍu, in the city of Virāṭa, the (Kuru forces) were routed and fled in all directions — that is sufficient proof."

sanskrit: balaṃ vīryaṃ ca tejaś ca śīghratā laghuhastatā aviṣādaś ca dhairyaṃ ca pārthān nānyatra vidyate
english: "Strength, valour, energy, swiftness, lightness of hand, undepressedness, and steadiness — these are found in the Pārthas (Pāṇḍavas) and nowhere else."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ity abravīd dhṛṣīkeśaḥ pārtham uddharṣayan girā garjan samayavarṣīva gagane pākaśāsanaḥ
english: Sañjaya said: Thus spoke Hrishikesha (Kṛṣṇa), exhilarating Pārtha with his words, thundering like Indra (Pākaśāsana) raining in the proper season in the sky.

sanskrit: keśavasya vacaḥ śrutvā kirīṭī śvetavāhanaḥ arjunas tan mahad vākyam abravīl lomaharṣaṇam
english: Having heard Keśava's words, Arjuna — the diademed one (Kirīṭī), the white-horsed — spoke that great speech which causes the hair to stand on end.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca saṃjayasya vacaḥ śrutvā prajñācakṣur nareśvaraḥ tataḥ saṃkhyātum ārebhe tad vaco guṇadoṣataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard Sañjaya's words, the lord of men whose eyes are wisdom (Dhṛtarāṣṭra) then began to weigh those words according to their merits and defects.

sanskrit: prasaṃkhyāya ca saukṣmyeṇa guṇadoṣān vicakṣaṇaḥ yathāvan matitattvena jayakāmaḥ sutān prati
english: And having calculated subtly the merits and defects, that discerning one — wishing for victory and thinking truly according to his understanding — with regard to his sons,

sanskrit: balābale viniścitya yāthātathyena buddhimān śaktiṃ saṃkhyātum ārebhe tadā vai manujādhipaḥ
english: Having ascertained the strength and weakness of each truly and accurately, that wise lord of men then began to reckon (their) power.

sanskrit: devamānuṣayoḥ śaktyā tejasā caiva pāṇḍavān kurūñ śaktyālpatarayā duryodhanam athābravīt
english: Having weighed the Pāṇḍavas by the power and energy belonging to both gods and men, and the Kurus as having lesser power, he then spoke to Duryodhana.
